clues.title: Plate: short, blue or green tinge when blurred
text: Guatemala has short licence plates, which when blurred will typically have either a blue tinge, or a hint of green on the left side.
clues.summary: Short plates that look blue, or slightly green on the left side, once blurred.

clues.title: Google car: grey with roof rack and mirrors
text: This **grey** Street View car with a visible roof rack and side mirrors can be seen on all car coverage in Guatemala.

NOTE: The only other tropical country with a similar car is [Laos](https://maps.app.goo.gl/uMGhM4Th1yi9GsaT9). The car used in the [Dominican Republic](https://goo.gl/maps/Hjv6G6xFYJm1F38i6) may look similar, but has thick black stripes on the bars and the mirrors are not visible.
clues.summary: A grey car with a roof rack and visible side mirrors, on all car coverage. Only Laos has a similar car.

differs.how: Laos has a similar grey car but a different landscape
Dominican car has thick black stripes on bars, mirrors hidden
Curaçao car has a black front

clues.title: Landscape: tropical, rainforest
text: Guatemala is a **tropical country**, and is mainly covered by rainforests.
clues.summary: A tropical country, mostly covered by rainforest.

clues.title: Houses: pastel stone, rusty metal roofs
text: Guatemalan architecture mainly consists of pastel painted stone houses, commonly with rusted sheet metal roofs. It is also somewhat common for buildings to be made out of exposed white brick.
clues.summary: Pastel-painted stone houses, often with rusty sheet metal roofs. Exposed white brick buildings are fairly common too.

clues.title: Road lines: thin, single yellow centre line
text: Similarly to Mexico, Guatemalan roads generally have solid white outer lines with a **single yellow middle line**. Road lines in Guatemala are generally significantly **thinner** than in [Mexico](https://www.google.com/maps/@15.684137,-92.0520015,3a,67.2y,89.22h,61.96t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sAWSMGxU5u0okOM9sg-Ah0g!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: Solid white edge lines with a single yellow centre line, like Mexico, but noticeably thinner than Mexican lines.

differs.how: Mexican road lines are much thicker

clues.title: Sign: stop sign says ALTO
text: Like Mexico, Panama and Costa Rica, Guatemala uses the word “**ALTO**” on stop signs.
clues.summary: Stop signs read ALTO, as in Mexico, Panama and Costa Rica.

clues.title: Pole: painted pink, green or both
text: In Guatemala you will very commonly see poles painted with either **pink**, **green** or a combination of the two.
clues.summary: Poles are very often painted pink, green, or a mix of both.

clues.title: Coverage: sparse, especially in the north
text: Guatemala has a fairly **low amount of coverage**, particularly in the north. Here you can see which roads are covered.
clues.summary: Not much coverage, especially in the north. Check which roads are covered on the map.

clues.title: Landscape: mountainous middle, flat ends
text: This is a topographic map of Guatemala. Generally speaking, the middle of the country is mountainous, while the south and north are fairly flat.
clues.summary: The middle of the country is mountainous, while the south and north are fairly flat.

clues.title: Landscape: completely flat farmland, built up
text: The southern regions of Guatemala mainly consist of **completely flat** agricultural land. It is generally more built up than flat areas in the [north](https://www.google.com/maps/@16.6546485,-90.1707062,3a,90y,317.32h,87t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sk183E0zMqWnu74AJOcvOFQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).
clues.summary: The south is completely flat farmland and more built up than the flat north.

clues.title: Landscape: mountainous centre
text: The central regions of Guatemala are generally **mountainous**.
clues.summary: The central part of the country is generally mountainous.

clues.title: Landscape: fairly flat with gentle hills
text: The northern regions of Guatemala are typically **fairly flat**. You will however usually see some hills or a slightly [rolling landscape](https://goo.gl/maps/gn49EV7aAQv94cq6A), rather than the complete flatness of the south.
clues.summary: The north is fairly flat but slightly rolling, unlike the completely flat south.

clues.title: Plants: oil palm plantations
text: **Oil palm plantations** are primarily found in two general areas: in the southwest and just north of the central mountain range.
clues.summary: Oil palm plantations are mainly in the southwest and just north of the central mountains.

clues.title: Pole: fully green, with small plates
text: **Completely green utility poles** are primarily found in the southeast of the country, but also on a road in the further north in the east and on a small stretch of road around Melchor de Mencos, near the end of the coverage in the far northeast.
These poles also feature small [pole plates](https://goo.gl/maps/sw6JyNjNerwDncwx8), which can further narrow down the road. This will be further explained in the next tip.
clues.summary: Fully green utility poles are mostly in the southeast, plus one road in the east and a stretch near the far northeast. They carry small plates that help find the road.

clues.title: Pole: green with white plate, road code
text: Most green utility poles contain a **white pole plate**, for which the **top two characters** will determine which road you are on. These roads and their corresponding characters are shown in this infographic.
clues.summary: Most green poles have a white plate. Its first two characters tell you which road you are on.

clues.title: Google car: top right bar faces forward
text: In most of the Guatemala coverage, the [top right bar](/images/guatemala/top_right_bar.png?) will be **facing forward**. This means that you can see [this line](/images/guatemala/zoomedinbar_line_highlighted.png?) on the side facing forward.
clues.summary: On most coverage the bar at the top right of the car points forward, so you see a line on its front-facing side.

clues.title: Google car: top right bar faces backward
text: The opposite is true in southeastern Guatemala, where the line is facing backwards.
clues.summary: In the southeast the same bar points backward instead, so that line is not on the forward-facing side.

clues.title: Google car: blue rope on bottom right bar
text: In these regions, you can often see a **blue rope** on the bottom right bar.

NOTE: Sometimes it can be [hard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/at4smsdgVk8HbsGaA) or [almost impossible](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HPXi6nrvanWVH3kk8) to see, in which case it might look like a normal backward facing bar.
clues.summary: In those backward-bar regions you can often see a blue rope on the bottom right bar. It can be hard to see, and then it just looks like a normal backward bar.

clues.title: Google car: bottom bar missing black cap
text: These regions in the south and northeast also have the backwards facing bar. The difference here is that the bottom right bar is **missing** the **thin black cap**, which is present in the other regions.
clues.summary: In the south and northeast, the bar also faces backward, but the bottom right bar is missing its thin black cap seen elsewhere.

clues.title: Phone numbers: start with 2
text: Phone numbers starting with a **2** are unique to Guatemala City.
clues.summary: Phone numbers starting with 2 are only found in the capital, Guatemala City.

clues.title: Phone numbers: start with 6
text: Similarly, phone numbers starting with a **6** are unique to the Guatemala Department.
NOTE: Phone numbers starting with 7 are found anywhere except for Guatemala Department, and phones starting with 3, 4 or 5 can be found anywhere in the country.
clues.summary: Numbers starting with 6 belong to Guatemala Department only. Numbers starting with 7 are everywhere except there, and 3, 4 or 5 can be anywhere.

clues.title: Landscape: huge lake among volcanoes
text: Lago de Atitlán is by far the **largest lake** in the mountainous regions of Guatemala. It is surrounded by mountains, and some volcanoes.
clues.summary: Lago de Atitlán is by far the largest lake in the mountains, surrounded by mountains and some volcanoes.

clues.title: Landscape: small dirt road in dense jungle
text: A **small dirt road** in the middle of a **dense jungle** can be found north of Tikal, in the far north of the country.
clues.summary: A small dirt road through dense jungle, north of Tikal in the far north.

clues.title: Bollard: small white, two black stripes
text: These small **white bollards** with **two black stripes** can be found on road 1 northeast of Quetzaltenango.
clues.summary: Small white bollards with two black stripes, found on road 1 northeast of Quetzaltenango.

clues.title: Road: rolling land, straight north-south
text: The PET-11, south of Las Pozas can be recognised by the slightly rolling landscape combined with its completely **north-to-south road angle**.
clues.summary: The PET-11 south of Las Pozas has gently rolling land and a road that runs straight north to south.

clues.title: Road: divided highway on concrete
text: The CA9, going between Escuintla and the coast, can be recognised by being a **divided highway** with **concrete pavement**.
clues.summary: The CA9 between Escuintla and the coast is a divided highway with concrete pavement.

clues.title: Coverage: trekker among Mayan temples
text: A trekker featuring several **Mayan temples** can be found just west of the town of Tikal.

It is worth mentioning that while there are other Guatemalan trekkers featuring [Mayan ruins](https://goo.gl/maps/fTti23Fq4zrCGzUE6), this is by far the most prominent and contains the largest and most intact temple structures.
clues.summary: A walking trekker with several Mayan temples, just west of Tikal. It has the biggest and most intact temples of any trekker here.

clues.title: Pole: white 'electricista' sticker
text: These white rectangular stickers that have the word **‘electricista’** written on them are unique to Guatemala City.

images.caption: Close-up of a white electrician sticker with a phone number on a pole

clues.summary: Rectangular white stickers reading 'electricista' on poles are only in Guatemala City.
